profile.name: Swapnil Mukherjee
profile.title: Technical Consultant @ Okta
profile.headline: I build the identity layer behind modern apps, from CIAM at scale to IAM for AI agents.
profile.shortBio: Technical Consultant at Okta helping enterprises design and deploy secure CIAM and IAM architectures, including identity patterns for AI agents, OAuth/OIDC, MFA, and Zero Trust access.
profile.about: Five years across enterprise identity — from federating 100+ applications onto Okta at a healthcare company with 22,000 workforce identities, to owning production Auth0 ops for Fifth Third Bank’s Newline platform and designing its migration to Ping Identity. Now on the platform side at Okta, I help enterprises design and deploy secure CIAM from the ground up: authentication flows, authorization models, MFA, extensibility, and the emerging identity patterns that AI agents require.
profile.availability: Always up for a conversation about identity architecture, CIAM challenges, or AI agent security.

projects.title: TripShare
projects.summary: Smart carpooling platform with route-matching algorithms and full-stack user management.
projects.description: TripShare tackles the last-mile coordination problem in carpooling by matching travelers with overlapping itineraries in real time. The platform was built end-to-end: a route-matching algorithm compares origin–destination pairs and time windows to surface compatible rides, while a full user-management layer handles registration, profiles, and trip history. A CMS-backed admin interface lets operators monitor active trips and flag disputes, and a CI/CD pipeline on GitHub Actions keeps deployments smooth across environments. Market-research-driven personas shaped the UX, ensuring the interface works for both frequent commuters and occasional ride-sharers.

projects.title: FAST Firmware Fuzzer
projects.summary: Advanced fuzzing framework that surfaces blind spots in firmware specifications and legacy systems.
projects.description: FAST Firmware Fuzzer extends SAFIREFUZZ, an academic mutation-based fuzzer, into a production-grade tool capable of surfacing specification blind spots that neither static analysis nor unit tests catch. It fuses three signal types — the device's formal specification, the compiled firmware binary, and its existing test suite — to intelligently mutate inputs and maximize code-path coverage in embedded targets. The framework resolves several upstream bugs that caused false negatives on edge-case inputs and adds integration shims for legacy systems that predate modern fuzzing harness conventions. Evaluation results were measured against a corpus of known firmware CVEs to validate detection recall.

projects.title: Pizzeria Manager
projects.summary: Java + SQL backend simulating store operations, inventory, and order processing.
projects.description: Pizzeria Manager is a full object-oriented simulation of a multi-location pizza chain's back-office operations, designed to stress-test data-modeling decisions at moderate scale. The Java codebase is organized around domain entities — orders, inventory SKUs, toppings, and staff shifts — each mapped to a normalized SQL schema with referential integrity enforced at the database layer. Multiple order types (dine-in, takeout, delivery) flow through a shared processing pipeline, and inventory levels are decremented transactionally to prevent oversell. The project served as a practical exercise in layered architecture, separating persistence, business logic, and presentation into independent, testable modules.

projects.title: DROWN Attack
projects.summary: Executed the DROWN attack against SSLv2 servers to recover keys and demonstrate protocol risk.
projects.description: DROWN (Decrypting RSA with Obsolete and Weakened eNcryption) is a cross-protocol attack that exploits SSLv2's weak export-grade cipher suites to decrypt modern TLS sessions sharing the same RSA key pair. This project executed a full proof-of-concept assessment against a controlled SSLv2 server: leveraging the Bleichenbacher oracle to iteratively refine candidate plaintexts until the server's RSA private key material was recoverable. The implementation reproduced the 2016 disclosure methodology and quantified the number of oracle queries required under realistic network conditions. Mitigation steps — disabling SSLv2 globally, rotating affected key pairs, and enforcing separate key material per protocol — were documented and verified against a patched server configuration.

projects.title: Space Hangman
projects.summary: Flask + HTML5 web game that wires multiple external APIs into a celestial Hangman.
projects.description: Space Hangman reimagines the classic word game inside a NASA-themed universe, where every session pulls live data from external APIs to keep gameplay fresh. The Flask backend orchestrates calls to a celestial-object API for themed vocabulary, a space-image API for atmospheric visuals, and a hint API that surfaces fun astronomical facts mid-game. The HTML5/CSS frontend renders a responsive game board with progressive reveal animations for each incorrect guess, replacing the traditional gallows with a spacecraft-damage sequence. Session state is managed server-side so players can resume interrupted games, and a leaderboard persists top scores across sessions.

projects.title: System Monitoring Tool
projects.summary: Python CLI for real-time tracking of CPU, memory, and network metrics with anomaly alerts.
projects.description: This Python CLI tool provides a real-time dashboard for system health, surfacing CPU utilization, per-core load distribution, memory pressure, swap usage, and interface-level network throughput in a single terminal view. Built on psutil for cross-platform metric collection and matplotlib for live chart rendering, it samples at a configurable interval and maintains a rolling window of historical readings. A rule-based alerting layer compares each sample against configurable thresholds and emits color-coded warnings when CPU load, memory usage, or packet error rates exceed acceptable bounds. The tool was designed to run headlessly on servers, outputting structured logs alongside the interactive display for post-hoc analysis.

projects.title: VoiceRx
projects.summary: Voice-driven EMR interface using Amazon Alexa to automate clinical data entry.
projects.description: VoiceRx addresses one of clinical computing's persistent pain points — manual data entry — by wiring Amazon Alexa into an Electronic Medical Records workflow. Clinicians dictate structured commands ("Record patient weight: 82 kilograms", "Flag allergy: penicillin") and the Alexa skill parses intent via a custom NLU model before writing the structured payload to the EMR via a REST API. The backend validates inputs against the patient's active record, prevents duplicate entries, and returns a spoken confirmation so the clinician can continue without breaking sterile field or eye contact with the patient. The system was prototyped against a sandbox EMR environment and evaluated for latency and recognition accuracy across medical terminology.

projects.title: HealthFit
projects.summary: Wellness app providing personalized daily caloric targets via REST APIs.
projects.description: HealthFit takes a user's current weight, target weight, activity level, and timeline and translates those inputs into a personalized daily caloric target backed by the Mifflin–St Jeor equation and activity multipliers grounded in published nutritional research. The Python backend exposes a clean REST API secured with OAuth 2.0, allowing third-party fitness apps to query recommendations on behalf of authenticated users. Input validation enforces clinically sensible bounds — rejecting deficit targets that fall below safe thresholds — and the response payload includes a breakdown of recommended macronutrient ratios alongside the total caloric figure. The project was designed to be extensible: adding a new goal type (muscle gain, maintenance) requires only a new calculation strategy, leaving the API contract unchanged.

projects.title: TweetFeel
projects.summary: NLP sentiment engine using RNNs to extract emotional structure from tweets.
projects.description: TweetFeel is an end-to-end NLP sentiment-analysis system built to extract nuanced emotional structure from short, noisy social-media text. The pipeline begins with a custom preprocessing stage that strips URLs, normalizes slang, and handles emoji transliteration before feeding cleaned text into learned word embeddings. A bidirectional RNN (GRU variant) then captures long-range dependencies across the token sequence, outputting a probability distribution across six emotional categories — joy, sadness, anger, fear, surprise, and neutral — rather than the coarser positive/negative binary common in simpler models. The model was trained and evaluated on a labeled tweet corpus, with attention-weight visualization added to surface which tokens drove each classification.

projects.title: Neural Style Transfer
projects.summary: Deep-learning app that fuses content and style images for art and therapeutic use.
projects.description: This project implements Gatys et al.'s neural style transfer algorithm from scratch in Python, using a pre-trained VGG-19 network as the feature extractor for both content and style representations. Content loss is computed from a deep convolutional layer to preserve high-level structure, while style loss is derived from Gram matrices across multiple shallower layers to capture texture and color palette without imposing spatial structure. An L-BFGS optimizer iteratively updates a noise-initialized canvas until it minimizes the weighted sum of both losses, converging on an image that reads as the content scene rendered in the chosen artistic style. The project explored therapeutic applications — pairing patients' personal photographs with calming artistic styles as a non-pharmacological anxiety-reduction tool.

projects.title: IoT Home Automation
projects.summary: Java-based NodeMCU firmware enabling remote control of traditional appliances.
projects.description: This project retrofits traditional household appliances with network connectivity using NodeMCU (ESP8266) microcontrollers flashed with custom Java-compatible firmware, bridging the gap between legacy hardware and modern smart-home ecosystems at minimal cost. Each NodeMCU unit connects to the home Wi-Fi network and registers with a lightweight MQTT broker, exposing appliance state (on/off, schedule, power reading) as subscribable topics. A Java control application on the local network subscribes to device topics and publishes command messages, allowing remote toggling, schedule programming, and state monitoring from any device on the LAN. The system was designed with non-technical users in mind: appliances appear as named entities in the control UI rather than raw MQTT topics, and a simple physical button always retains manual override.

projects.title: Fraud Detection
projects.summary: ML pipeline using K-Nearest Neighbour tuned for highly imbalanced credit-transaction data.
projects.description: This credit-card fraud detector addresses the fundamental challenge of extreme class imbalance — fraudulent transactions typically represent less than 0.2% of real-world datasets — by combining careful feature engineering with a tuned K-Nearest Neighbours classifier optimized for recall over accuracy. Custom distance metrics weight transaction velocity, geographic anomalies, and merchant category codes more heavily than raw amounts, reflecting domain knowledge about how fraudsters operate. SMOTE oversampling is applied to the minority class during training to prevent the model from defaulting to the majority class, and hyperparameter search explores K values, distance functions, and weighting schemes across cross-validation folds. Final evaluation uses precision-recall curves and F2 score (which penalizes missed fraud more than false alarms) rather than standard accuracy, better reflecting the asymmetric cost of each error type.
